newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian state offering 40 pct of housing firm.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian state offering 40 pct of housing firm.

text.p: The Egyptian state's Holding Company for Housing, Tourism and Cinema announced on Saturday that it wanted to sell 40 percent of the shares in Cairo Housing and Development to one or more strategic investors.
The price for the 2.544 million shares will be the market price on the Egyptian stock exchange at the end of the last trading day before the announcement -- 24.40 pounds a share.

Applicants must apply for at least 20 percent of the shares on sale and preference will go to those who seek the most, it said. The deadline for applications is noon (0900 GMT) on Sunday, September 15, it added.
The holding company, which now owns 79.5 percent of the 6.36 million shares in Cairo Housing and Development, may sell more than 40 percent of the shares, it said.
Other shareholders include banks and public-sector companies (8.75 percent) and private-sector investors (11.75 percent).

Cairo Housing and Development made a net after-tax profit of 2.947 million pounds in the financial year 1994/5 and paid a dividend of 0.48 pounds. The holding company said new shareholders would receive the 1995/6 dividend but it did not give the housing company's results for that financial year.
When the 1995/6 year ended on June 30, Cairo Housing and Development had reserves of 9.929 million pounds, down from 12.030 million a year earlier.
